audit.why: 47.32% Emerald+, HARD at 7/10. Tahm Kench out-ranges Kassadin 900 to 650 with Tongue Lash, converts three An Acquired Taste stacks into a point-and-click stun, and — unusually for a tank — keeps answering Kassadin's pattern into the late game because Devour removes the assassination target. The mirrored Tahm Kench audit reaches the same conclusion from his side.

Tahm Kench at Levels 1 through 4-5, Skill at Level 6, Tahm Kench at First item and Two+ items, on both layers, with captions that match. The mirrored Tahm Kench page calls Level 6 'an even skirmish window' — the same Skill row from the other side, so the two directions agree without correction. Spikes are Lvl 1-3, Lvl 6, 1st item and Late, which is the same curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors, all of which the mirrored Tahm Kench audit also had to fix from the other side. (a) Devour is treated as an early-game threat: early warns of 'a Q-stun-into-Devour that just deletes you before 6', whys[1] describes it at Level 2, whys[2] at Level 3, and wants.foe[0] says 'then Devour for a kill before you hit 6'. Devour is his ultimate and does not exist before 6. (b) Grey health is credited to Devour — 'his Thick Skin and Devour grey-heal the chunk you land', 'heal the chunk back with grey health from Devour and Thick Skin'. Riot puts the whole mechanic on Thick Skin: 'Tahm Kench stores a percent of the damage he takes and heals based on it while out of combat. Active: Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield', 3s cooldown. Devour on an enemy is magic damage; on an ally it is a shield. (c) late, whys[6] and spikes[3] claim 'his percent-max-HP Q and W damage cut straight through your passive's 15% magic reduction'. Riot's An Acquired Taste text is 'gaining extra damage based on his total health' — his health, not a percentage of yours — and nothing in his kit is described as bypassing resistances or reduction. The mirrored audit establishes the opposite and better fact: Devour deals magic damage, so Void Stone is a standing discount on his ultimate.
audit.why: Point (c) is the one that changes how the page reads. It told a Kassadin his defining passive is worthless in this matchup when it is one of the few things working for him.
audit.corrected: Devour is now explicitly the ultimate that joins at 6, with the three-stack Tongue Lash stun as the pre-6 punish; grey health belongs to Thick Skin and its 3s conversion; and Void Stone is credited with discounting Devour rather than being bypassed.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says 'Use R to dive under map and travel cross-lane, snowballing other lanes while you farm defensively'.
audit.why: That is Abyssal Voyage, the pre-rework ultimate, which the live champion does not have — the same removed-ability error the mirrored Tahm Kench audit found on his page. His current R is Devour and it has no map-travel component; the dive is Abyssal Dive (W), 21/20/19/18/17s at 1000-1200 range.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to Abyssal Dive on 21s as the re-engage and Devour as the tool that saves the carry you want dead.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged no cooldown sequencing, and the full layer points every green light at Abyssal Dive's cooldown, which is not what gates the thing that kills you.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s at 900 range against your 650 — that 250-unit gap is the early lane. Abyssal Dive is 21s. Devour has no listed cooldown at all; what gates it on you is carrying three An Acquired Taste stacks. So the clock a Kassadin counts is his own stack count, not one of Tahm Kench's timers.
audit.corrected: Own-stack-count is now the tracked clock in winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], report[9], dosFull[1].t and loading, with Tongue Lash's 7s/900 range and Abyssal Dive's 21s stated alongside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Several fields tell you to 'blink out of his Q-stun'; breakdown.late claims a 'Q-silence'.
audit.why: A stunned Kassadin cannot cast Riftwalk — the blink has to be spent before the stun connects, not after, and the page never said so. Null Sphere has no silence; Riot's text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels'.
audit.corrected: Blink timing is now 'leave before the third-stack stun lands, because a stunned Kassadin cannot cast anything'; the silence claim is replaced with the interrupt.

edits.before: Tahm Kench punishes your worst stage hard. His passive, Acquired Taste, stacks on you with every auto and Q, and the third stack turns his next Tongue Lash into a stun - so once he's loaded the stacks, one Q locks you down for a free trade or an all-in you can't answer with just Null Sphere. Your Q poke barely matters because his Thick Skin and Devour grey-heal the chunk you land, and your mana pool can't afford to keep chucking it. Last-hit at max range, watch your Acquired-Taste stacks, and never walk into Q range with three stacks on you - that's the cue for a Q-stun-into-Devour that just deletes you before 6.
edits.after: Tahm Kench punishes your worst stage hard. An Acquired Taste stacks on you with every auto and Tongue Lash, and the third stack makes his next Tongue Lash a stun — so once you are loaded, one Q locks you down for a free trade you cannot answer with Null Sphere alone. Range is the other half of it: Tongue Lash reaches 900 to your 650, so he chips you for free. Your poke barely matters either, because Thick Skin banks the damage he takes and converts it into a shield on a 3-second cooldown. Last-hit at max range, count your own stacks, and never step into Q range carrying three. Devour is his ultimate — the pre-6 punish is the stun, not a swallow.

edits.before: You're still weathering it through 4-5 - Nether Blade's mana restore keeps you farming under tower, but you have no kill pressure on a champ who grey-heals your damage. Level 6 is the one moment you breathe: Riftwalk lets you blink out of his Q-stun and the Devour windup that defined the early game, so you stop dying to the all-in. Don't mistake it for a fight window - you can't burst a Tahm Kench, you can only stop being eaten by him. Use 6 to dodge his stun, escape ganks, and start farming for real.
edits.after: You're still weathering it through 4-5 - Nether Blade's mana restore keeps you farming under tower, but you have no kill pressure on a champion who banks your damage as grey health and converts it with Thick Skin every 3 seconds. Level 6 is the one moment you breathe: Riftwalk lets you leave before the three-stack Tongue Lash stun lands, so you stop dying to the all-in — and it only works before the stun, because a stunned Kassadin cannot cast anything at all. Don't mistake it for a fight window; use 6 to dodge, escape ganks and farm for real.

edits.before: This is where it stays bad even after you scale. Your whole late-game identity is blinking in to assassinate squishies, but Tahm exists to deny exactly that - his Devour swallows your target (or himself) out of your Riftwalk burst, his stacked Q stuns you mid-engage, and his percent-max-HP Q and W damage cut straight through your passive's 15% magic reduction. Your Riftwalk dives rarely land clean on a carry he's babysitting. Don't try to 1v1 him; play for picks elsewhere on the map and let your team peel his tongue while you delete everyone he isn't guarding.
edits.after: This is where it stays bad even after you scale. Your whole late-game identity is blinking in to assassinate squishies, and Tahm exists to deny exactly that — Devour swallows your target (or himself) out of your Riftwalk burst, and his stacked Tongue Lash stuns you mid-engage. One thing does run your way: Devour deals magic damage, so Void Stone's 15% reduction is a standing discount on his ultimate. Your dives still rarely land clean on a carry he's babysitting, so don't 1v1 him — play for picks elsewhere and let your team peel his tongue while you delete everyone he isn't guarding.

notes: Mirror reuse: audits/top/tahmkench__kassadin.json was already written and I took its settled facts rather than re-deriving them — Tongue Lash 900 vs Null Sphere 650, Devour is the ultimate and not a pre-6 threat, Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than silencing, Riftwalk is 2-5s so mana rather than cooldown is its limit, and Devour deals magic damage so Void Stone discounts it. That last one is where the two pages had directly contradicted each other: his page said Void Stone is a standing discount on Devour, mine said his damage 'cuts straight through your passive's 15% magic reduction'. Mine was wrong and is now aligned. The Abyssal Voyage error appears on both sides — his page in mid, mine in wants.foe[2] — and both are now Abyssal Dive. The level chart needed no change; it already agreed with the mirror on Level 6 being the Skill row.
